recipe.name: Multigrain Spelt Sourdough
directions: Build the liquid levain (everything listed in the Levain Build section above) in the morning or afternoon and store somewhere around 78°F (25°C) ambient for 5 hours to ripen. It should be well fermented, expanded, and have a smell that’s slightly sour, perhaps with a hint of sweetness.

Mix flour and water (reserve 100g water for the mix, later) in a bowl until all dry bits are hydrated. Cover the bowl and store somewhere nice and warm for 1 hour. Somewhere near your levain is convenient.

Add the called for ripe levain and diastatic malt powder to the autolysed dough and using about half of the reserved 100g of water mix thoroughly by hand. The levain should be well mixed through the dough and the added water wholly absorbed.
Let the dough rest for 20 minutes before adding salt.

When finished mixing and resting, sprinkle the salt on top of the dough and the remaining water to help dissolve. Pinch through the dough thoroughly and fold the dough over itself to help incorporate and absorb the remaining water. Keep pinching and folding until all the water is absorbed and the dough comes back together.
Transfer the dough to a tub or thick-walled bowl for the first rise: bulk fermentation.

At 78°F (25°C) ambient temperature, bulk fermentation should go for about 4 hours. Perform three sets of gentle stretch and folds during bulk, spaced out by 30 minutes. After the third set of stretch and folds let the dough rest for the remainder of bulk.
